findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` may return nil (user never interacted with the topic, or is anonymous so current_user is nil). `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError, producing a 500. Also `current_user.id` raises when not logged in, since unsubscribe is in the ensure_logged_in list only for the normal path; the lookup should handle a missing record, e.g. with TopicUser.change.

findings.title: unsubscribe toggles state in a non-idempotent way and ignores the intended action
findings.body: The action flips the notification level: if currently above regular it sets regular, otherwise sets muted. Clicking an email unsubscribe link twice (or a mail client prefetch/scanner following the GET link) will alternate between muted and regular, re-subscribing the user. An unsubscribe link should set muted deterministically.

findings.title: unsubscribe bypasses guardian checks and uses raw params for lookup
findings.body: TopicView.new is built with params[:topic_id] which may be a slug-less id, and the TopicUser update uses params[:topic_id] directly without ensuring the topic is visible to the current user. Notifications are then changed for a topic the user may not be able to see; guardian.ensure_can_see! should be applied.

findings.title: unsubscribe GET is state-changing and exempt from check_xhr and CSRF-protected flow
findings.body: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates state on GET (and skip_before_filter :check_xhr is added), so any third-party page can trigger a muted change through an image or link for logged-in users (CSRF-like). Mutations should require POST or a signed token.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url is hardcoded to the topic path and ignores the post number and slug
findings.body: unsubscribe_url builds "#{url}/unsubscribe" from url(), which uses the current slug. Routes also add "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" but the mailer now emits the slug form with `url` which may be a stale slug; the value is not validated against the actual route in the email, and the user_notifications path passes this URL into an email whose unsubscribe_link i18n key is also used by digest emails that do not provide unsubscribe_url, potentially rendering a broken %{unsubscribe_url} placeholder.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now references %{unsubscribe_url} for all emails
findings.body: The shared unsubscribe_link string now contains %{unsubscribe_url}. Emails that add the unsubscribe link without passing unsubscribe_url (e.g. digest, admin or other MessageBuilder users with add_unsubscribe_link) will hit I18n interpolation errors or emit the literal placeholder text.

findings.title: html template still uses %{unsubscribe_link} placeholder instead of the new per-topic link text
findings.body: The template keeps only the generic %{unsubscribe_link} placeholder; the per-topic link text was added to the text/locale only, so the HTML email never shows the topic-specific unsubscribe option. Also `%{respond_instructions}` is now inside a div that previously had line breaks, which changes rendering but is minor.

findings.title: misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (extra 'i'), and the template references the same misspelling, so it works internally but the name is a typo that will confuse future maintainers and any other references.

findings.title: unsubscribe strings contain HTML and unclear copy
findings.body: stop_notifications contains raw <strong> markup inside a client string rendered with triple-stash in the template; the change_notification_state string lacks a trailing period, inconsistent with the other messages. Also the diff removes a blank line from an unrelated section.

findings.title: unrelated formatting churn in topic_user.rb
findings.body: Large whitespace and reformatting changes (scope, create_lookup, track_visit!) are unrelated to the unsubscribe feature and make review harder without functional benefit.

findings.title: no tests for unsubscribe controller action or per-topic unsubscribe link
findings.body: The only test change adds an unsubscribe_url option to a builder spec. No request spec covers the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (mute/regular toggle, redirect, slug mismatch, anonymous access), and the message builder spec does not assert that the body contains the topic unsubscribe URL.
